I've got 15 mu and two pairs of hands in this house — mine and my wife's. I'm 66 now, so I farm the same way every year. What worked last year, I do again. Change is what gets you a bad harvest.

Ten mu I do wheat in winter and corn in summer, like my father did, like everyone in the village does. Five mu I keep for cotton. I would grow more cotton because it pays better, but cotton needs many sprayings and picking by hand — too much work for us old people. Five mu is my limit.

For wheat, before planting I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind the dealer sells, one bag is about 80 jin. Then in spring when the wheat turns green and stands up, I throw 1 bag of urea per mu. My neighbor Old Zhang does the same and gets 900 jin per mu most years. I water from my well 3 times — before winter freeze, at green-up, and when the grain fills. If spring is dry I water a 4th time. I spray twice, once when the little bugs come on the leaves, once near flowering for the rust.

Corn I plant right after wheat harvest, no plowing — just drop the seed in. Hybrid seed from the dealer, same variety the village uses. One bag compound at sowing, one bag urea when corn reaches my knee. Water twice, spray once for corn borer. Usually 1100 jin per mu, good years more.

Cotton is the hardest. Bt cotton seed — the dealer says it handles the bollworm better, and it's true, less spraying than before. Still I spray about 6 times through summer, every 10-12 days when bolls form. 2 bags compound at planting, 1 bag urea when flowering starts. Water 4 times from the well. I hire the tractor man for rotary tillage — my back can't do the plowing anymore. Seed cotton maybe 450-500 jin per mu.

Fertilizer is my biggest worry — every year it costs more. But I would rather buy an extra bag than see yellow leaves. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting a few yuan of fertilizer is just a cost.
